comment: Source identity: EP260429a / GRB 260429B. Adopted T0 is the EP-WXT transient onset in GCN 44426, 2026-04-29 14:41:11 UTC. The previous bot value 2026-04-29T23:24:02Z instead matches the unrelated Fermi GBM event GRB260429975 in external/fermi_gbm (RA 283.92 deg, Dec +18.1 deg), not this source; GCN 44429 also identifies that separate event as Fermi GRB 260429A. Trigger_Instrument corrected from SVOM/C-GFT to Einstein Probe/WXT. Adopted coordinates are the COLIBRÍ optical counterpart candidate in GCN 44738 (RA 240.58812, Dec -9.60116; quoted uncertainty 0.5 arcsec, confidence level unstated); GCN 44445 reports the likely X-ray afterglow EPF_J160221.2-093607 at a consistent position. The candidate is offset about 2.55 arcmin from the WXT centroid in GCN 44426; its association is suggested by fading and spatial coincidence with the likely FXT afterglow, not yet confirmed. GCN 44443 gives AstroSat CZTI T90=34 (+6/-9) s; sub_tag=lgrb follows that catalog T90 classification. GCN 44434 title/event identify GRB 260429B / EP260429a, although one body sentence says “EP GRB 260429A”; treated as a body typo, not a separate source. Photometry search (2026-11-02): repository gcn/archive is absent; external/rssgrbag lightcurve snapshot has 139 rows and no 260429 match; external/grbsn_webtool/SourceData has no matching event directory. GCN site/event pages for EP260429a and GRB 260429B yielded 7 related circulars reviewed (44426, 44433, 44434, 44437, 44443, 44445, 44738); optical measurements/limits were added or retained as detailed per-row. Exact-name public web searches found no research paper result, but ADS/SciX API search remains limited because no API credential is available; this is not evidence that no literature exists. Search result: of the 7 GCN circulars reviewed, 5 LC rows were newly added and the 4 pre-existing rows were reviewed and updated; ADS/SciX remains unresolved.
